comparisons.peer_topic: Co-involvement and derivatives in specific loan types
comparisons.peer_summary: For commercial mortgage loans, the Firm often transfers only a portion of assets to the SPE while unrelated parties provide the rest; for residential mortgage loans, the Firm may enter into interest rate swaps or caps with the SPE.
comparisons.comparison: Both Bank of America and Morgan Stanley disclose details regarding the structure and mechanics of their agency and commercial mortgage securitization transactions, specifically focusing on the transfer of assets to Special Purpose Entities (SPEs). Bank of America reports the financial outcome of these activities through the deconsolidation of trusts (e.g., $1.1 billion in assets in 2024). In contrast, Morgan Stanley details the operational mechanism of these transactions, noting that for commercial mortgage loans, it often transfers only a portion of assets to the SPE while unrelated parties provide the remainder, and for residential mortgages, it may enter into derivative transactions with the SPE. While both discuss mortgage securitizations and the role of SPEs, BAC focuses on the consolidation status and asset volume removed from its balance sheet, whereas MS focuses on the asset sharing and derivative involvement within the securitization structure.

sentences.text: During 2024, 2023 and 2022, the Corporation deconsolidated agency residential mortgage securitization trusts with total assets of $1.1 billion, $685 million and $784 million.
In many securitization transactions involving commercial mortgage loans, the Firm transfers a portion of the assets to the SPE with unrelated parties transferring the remaining assets.

In addition, mainly in securitization transactions involving residential mortgage loans, the Firm may also enter into derivative transactions, primarily interest rate swaps or interest rate caps, with the SPE.
